newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover soars in week to Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover soars in week to Jan 17.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) saw a 76.6 percent rise in its turnover during the week to January 17 due to a bigger sale of the central bank bonds and wheat contracts, the bourse said on Monday.
Total BSE turnover stood at 44.211 million dinars ($8.43 million) in 170 transactions, up on 25.032 million dinars in 134 deals a week ago.

"BSE turnover rose after the central bank auctioned a new tranche of its 30-day bonds offering them at a record high interest rate of an annual 147.48 percent," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
"Another encouraging sign for the bourse was that wheat forward contracts enjoyed a renewed investor interest," Stimac added.
Apart from those, the bourse performed amidst tight liquidity of the banking sector, with banks disposing of around 16 million dinars of surplus funds on Friday, traders said.
"It is difficult to work under such conditions. Now and then, a company comes in with modest funds but otherwise, revolving old borrowing is the key activity," a trader said.
For the week ending January 17, the BSE reported the following detail:
* Commercial paper traded 130 times, for a volume of 19.413 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 26 deals, worth 2.301 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 793 percent.
* Central bank short-term bonds traded three times for a volume of 11.2 million dinars.
* BSE reported nine deals in wheat contracts, worth 10.897 million dinars.
Wheat contracts accounted for around 18 percent of the total weekly turnover.
"Growing investor interest signals some things are not so bad in this terrible situation," an analyst said.
Buyers are mainly flour mills. "They find ways to obtain money and buy contracts, because the price of wheat is fixed at 0.9 dinars per kilo and the dinar rate is no longer stable," a trader said.
"People finally seem to know how to take advantage of this bourse and the paper providing them with a state guarantee and an export licence," the trader added.
